transcript.text: I can help you with that. When a dishwasher won't come on at all, it is often just a simple power issue like a tripped socket or a loose plug, though internal wiring faults are also possible. To check this safely, please ensure the machine is switched off and unplugged from the wall outlet. Then, try plugging another appliance into that same socket to confirm it has power, and make sure your dishwasher's plug is firmly seated in the back of the unit.
it's an integrated one, wired in, not a plug I can get at. other sockets and lights in the kitchen work fine. the switch above the worktop is on and its light is lit

Since you have confirmed the power supply is reaching the switch and other kitchen appliances are working, the issue likely lies with the dishwasher's internal wiring or controls rather than the home's electricity. To help me identify the correct parts or settings for your specific unit, could you please provide the make and model number? This information is usually found on a label located on the side edge of the door frame. If the door won't open to access this label right now, that is fine and we can look at other options later.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
it's a Neff. label on the door edge says S513G60X0G

Thanks for providing those details. Since your Neff S513G60X0G is hardwired and you have confirmed power at the switch, let's check if a safety feature has stopped it from starting. Please open the door and look around the rubber seal on the tub edge and along the bottom of the door for any splits or items caught in it that might be causing a leak. If the seal looks fine, try turning each spray arm by hand to ensure nothing is catching them or pointing water at the door.
I haven't looked, but it was fine yesterday and I haven't seen any leak. It's completely dead, no lights or display at all, so I don't see how a seal would matter. Is there something else to check?

Yes, there are a few other things we can look at since the power seems to be reaching the unit. First, please check if your dishwasher has a child lock or control lock enabled, as this often prevents the display from turning on even when the machine is powered. You might also want to see if there is a delay start programme currently selected, which would stop it from starting immediately. If neither of these is the case, we may need to look at the door latch mechanism to ensure it is fully engaging and clicking into place.
there's no display at all so no child lock or delay start showing. door is closed and latched firmly. nothing tripped at the consumer unit either. what else?

Since you have confirmed power at the switch and checked for common settings without success, we need to look deeper into the electrical connection inside the appliance. Because your Neff S513G60X0G is hardwired, it connects via a spur unit (often a switch above the worktop) or directly under the sink. Please ensure you have switched off the power at that spur unit and removed the access panel to check if the wires are secure in their terminals. If the wiring looks fine there, we may need to inspect the door wiring loom, as a broken wire inside the hinge flex is a common cause for a completely dead display on integrated models.

I'm not comfortable opening up the wiring and I can't pull the dishwasher out anyway. I don't have a meter or a spare fuse either. Is there anything else I can check from the outside, or should I get someone in?

It sounds like you should get someone in, as we have ruled out the simple power supply issues and settings. Since your Neff S513G60X0G is hardwired and completely dead with no display, and you are not comfortable checking the internal wiring or removing the unit to inspect the door loom, a qualified engineer is needed to diagnose this safely. The most likely causes for these symptoms—given that power reaches the switch but the machine won't start—are either an internal fault on the main control PCB or a broken wire in the door hinge flex that cuts off power to the display. An engineer can test these components and replace them if necessary.
